subject: alienFlora
pitch:
Category: Plant.
Subject: bioluminescent alien plant.
Style: Avatar.

spec.name: Pandoran Lumen Bloom
spec.description: A bioluminescent alien plant in the Avatar/Pandora style: an S-curved indigo stalk with glowing veins, a crown of eight arching veined fronds, hanging glowing tendrils and pods, and a ring of spiral fan flowers at its base.
spec.layout: A tall S-curved stalk stands at x=0,z=0 and rises from a flared root buttress at y=0 to a crown cup at y≈2.55. Eight broad leaf fronds radiate from the crown at 45° steps, rise to about y=3.1 and arch outward and down, so the canopy is about 2.8 m wide. A spiky central bud glows above the crown. Under the canopy, 10 glowing tendrils with bulb tips hang from a ring around the upper stalk, with 6 glowing seed pods on short stems at radius ~0.9. Five helicoradian spiral-fan plants form a front-biased arc at the base (+Z side) on short stems 0.5 to 0.9 m tall. Their glowing spiral fans can be opened or closed. Colours follow Pandora: a deep indigo-teal body lit by cyan, teal, violet, magenta and lime glow. Every glow colour (names starting 'glow' or 'spore') is wrapped in glow() from the glow kit, so the glowing parts read as self-lit against the dark body. The style shows as bulbous rounded masses ending in sharp tips, rows of small glowing dots along veins and edges, and a root-to-tip colour shift from dark indigo to bright teal to a glowing cyan edge. Dark body parts never glow. Glow is built as small parts seated on the surface: vein sweeps, dots, rings, edge trims. No ground, rocks or props anywhere.

parts.builds: The flared root buttress and ground contact. Four to six thick buttress roots sweep out from rootCollar to the floor and curl outward, in rootDark with rootMid highlights, each ending in a pointed tip that touches y=0. Small low moss patches (moss with mossLight tops) grow on the upward faces of the roots, and a few short surface rootlets reach out. Glowing veins (glowTeal sweeps, with rows of small glowCyan dots seated along the roots) run from the stalk base down each root and fade toward the tips. A dark knobbly collar ring around the stalk at rootCollar overlaps the trunk's base. Roots stay within radius ~1.3 and leave the front arc (z>0.5) mostly free for the helicoradians. Rides joint base.
parts.attaches: Covers the trunk's bottom at mount base and rootCollar. The trunk starts at y=0.5 inside the collar.

parts.builds: The S-curved main stalk and crown cup, as one skinned sweep or loft over the chain base, stalk1, stalk2, stalk3, crown through mounts base, stalk1, stalk2, stalk3, crown. Radius is about 0.36 at y=0.5, narrows to about 0.15 near y=1.5, swells slightly at stalk3 and flares into a cupped crown (lathe or flared loft with a lip at y≈2.6, radius ~0.34). The body is trunkDark with trunkMid lengthwise ridge bands and trunkLight highlights on the sun side. Raised knuckle rings (bulging nodes) at stalk1 and stalk2 are trunkMid. Glowing veins: three or four glowCyan and glowTeal thin sweeps spiral around the stalk, dotted with small round glowTeal beads at the knuckles, so the glow is brightest at the crown and fades toward the base. The crown cup has a glowViolet inner rim ring and a glowMagenta dot ring just below the lip. Stalk-mounted details are a few small leaf-scale bumps (leafDeep) and a couple of moss tufts at the lower trunk. No fronds, tendrils or roots here.
parts.attaches: Starts inside the root collar at rootCollar (y≈0.5). The crown cup at crown and crownRim carries the frond roots and the bud. The tendrilRing sits on the stalk at y≈2.3, and tendril chains parent to stalk3.

parts.builds: The canopy: eight broad, arching leaf fronds on joints frondA to frondH (each frond a 3 to 4 joint chain parented to its joint, named like frondA1..frondA3, role arm, group fronds) plus the central bud. Each frond is about 1.3 to 1.45 m long. It rises from crownRim, climbs to about y=3.1 around 40% of its length, then arches outward and droops to a pointed tip near y≈2.3. It is a wide lance or leaf shape (extruded or swept membrane, about 0.5 m at the widest, pointed tip with a slight curl) with flat colours by section: leafDeep at the root, leafMid in the middle, leafTip near the tip. Front and back faces differ: leafMid on top, leafDeep under with violet-tinged underside. Each frond has a raised midrib sweep (trunkLight) with a glowCyan vein line on top, 4 to 5 pairs of side veins in glowTeal branching toward the edge, and a thin glowCyan edge trim sweep. Rows of tiny glowLime or glowCyan dots seat along the veins, and each tip ends in a bright glowPink or glowCyan bead. Alternate fronds A, C, E, G with glowViolet vein accents and the others with glowTeal, so the canopy shifts colour around it. The central bud is a spiky closed-petal cone (5 to 7 overlapping pointed petals in leafMid and leafTip with glowMagenta tips), rising from the crown at crown to budTop (y≈3.15), with a glowPink core sphere showing between the petals and a few floating sporeWhite motes near it. Fronds are the hero silhouette: keep them readable and sharp-tipped.
parts.attaches: Frond roots start at the crown cup at crownRim and the frondA to frondH joints, parented to crown. The bud sits on crown at the cup's centre.

parts.builds: Hanging bioluminescent growth under the canopy, in the style of the Tree of Voices. 10 tendrils form a ring at tendrilRing (radius ~0.4 around the stalk at y≈2.3, parented to stalk3), each a 4 joint chain named tendril0..tendril9 plus joint index (role tentacle, group tendrils). Each hangs 1.0 to 1.5 m, drifting outward to radius 0.6 to 1.1, with lengths varied, never below y=0.95. Each is a thin tapered sweep (trunkMid at the root to leafMid at the tip) with a glowing spiral thread: alternating glowCyan and glowViolet beads along its length, and a bulb (a small icosphere with a ring of tiny sporeWhite dots) at its tip in glowTeal or glowMagenta. Six seed pods hang on short curved stems at radius ~0.9 and y 1.6 to 2.2: each a rounded teardrop in podShell with podMid lengthwise ribs, a glowing slit (glowMagenta or glowLime) down its front and a cap ring in trunkDark. Glow-spore motes (small sporeWhite and glowCyan low-poly spheres, 20 to 30 of them) drift in the airy space between tendrils at various heights between y=1.0 and y=2.6. Roots attach at the stalk ring, so a small trunkMid collar ring with glowViolet dots sits on the stalk at tendrilRing.
parts.attaches: The tendril roots sit on the stalk at tendrilRing (mount, on joint stalk3). Pod stems start from fronds' undersides near radius 0.8 or from the tendril ring. Nothing touches the floor.

parts.builds: Five Helicoradian-style spiral-fan plants in a front arc at the base, on joints helixA to helixE (each a 2 to 3 joint chain parented to its joint: helixA1.., role fan, group helix). Positions run along fanArc, from the left rear (-1.0,0.55) round the front (0,1.1) to (1.0,0.55). Each has a slim curved trunkMid stem 0.45 to 0.9 m tall (helixC the tallest at ~0.9 m, the outer ones shorter) with a bulb base in moss at the floor. At the top is a spiral fan: 10 to 14 thin feathery filament blades (swept thin tapered tubes or small extruded leaves) arranged in a spiral on a ring, tilted outward like a cone. Colour runs root to tip as leafDeep, leafMid and glowTeal at the tips, and each filament ends in a bead (glowCyan, glowViolet, glowMagenta or glowLime, a different dominant colour on each plant). A glowing glowPink centre bud sits at the middle of the fan. Fans are about 0.3 to 0.45 m across, shown open. A few small ground sprouts (stubby cones in moss with a glowLime tip, 6 to 8 of them) fill gaps between the plants, and moss tufts sit at the stem bases. Everything rests on the floor (stem bases touch y=0). Keep the roots' area free, so these sit in front of the buttress roots.
parts.attaches: Stem bases meet the floor in front of the buttress roots, parented to base. Nothing is built above y=1.15. The tallest fan stays below the tendrils' lowest point (y≈0.95 at radius 0.6 to 1.1), so keep fan tops at or below y=1.1 and their footprint at z≥0.3.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a spec for a bioluminescent alien plant in the Pandora style, drawing on ideas like spiral fan-worm structures and willow-like glowing tendrils. I'm leaning toward a composite: a central trunk-stalk with broad fronds carrying glowing veins, spiral fans clustered at the base, and drooping luminous tendrils.

I'm settling the scale at roughly 2.6 by 3.2 by 2.6, with a curved trunk, a canopy of large fronds, hanging tendrils, glowing spore pods, spiral fans, and a root buttress. For the joints, I'm planning a root base, a stack of stalk segments up the spine, and a crown, with the fronds, fans, and tendrils attached around it.

I'm laying out the parts of the plant as a set of five pieces, starting with a root base that has buttress roots, glowing root veins, and a mossy mound at the floor. Next I'm specifying the trunk, a ridged stalk running from about y 0.5 to the top, with spiraling glowing veins, ringed nodes, and a cupped crown at its peak.

I'm laying out the last parts of the plant: the frond ring, the tendrils and pods hanging from the crown, and the spiral fans, which I've only just started listing.

I'm now settling the rest of the spec: the fan cluster sits at the front base, with small stalks each carrying a spiral of glowing feathery rings, plus mini glowing mushrooms along the floor. I'm fixing the overall size at 2.8 wide, 3.2 high, and 2.8 long, and picking an Avatar-style palette of deep indigo, teal glows, magenta, and lime accents, starting with the trunk tones.

Still writing the palette and the joint mounts...

I'm placing the trunk's S-curve points and tying the crown and tendril rings to the trunk's top, with the trunk radius tapering from the base up to a flared crown cup. I'm starting to fix the joint chain from the root base up the spine.

Still working out the joint layout: the spine runs through the trunk stalks up to the crown, and I'm assigning the fan joints at the base and the frond joints in a ring at the top.

Still computing the frond positions around the crown, eight of them spaced evenly with outward and upward directions.

I'm working out the frond arrangement now: they arch outward and droop at the tips, and the crown carries a central glowing spire. Next I'm deciding whether the tendrils should hang from a ring on the crown's underside.

I'm working out the tendril layout now: ten strands hanging from a ring under the crown, drifting outward and stopping above the ground. I'm also adding glowing spore pods on short stems and small floating wisps around the trunk.

I'm finishing the visual style notes: soft bulbous organic forms with sharp tips, bioluminescent dot patterns, and emissive glow for the glowing colors, with a gradient running from root to tip through banded parts.
